18: POTÁPYCH. Your spite's always getting in its work. VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. Not spite, not spite, my friend! You're mistaken! I have just been so insulted that it's impossible to live in this world after it. I shall die, but I shall not forget.
17: POTÁPYCH. It must be she got out the wrong side of bed; she's out of sorts. [VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA rubs her hands with pleasure ] Here now, I see that you're happy; you're dying for some deviltry or other. Phew! Lord forgive us! What a disposition! VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. You are saying insulting words to me, Potápych, insulting to my very heart. When did I ever say anything about you to the mistress?
16: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. To wish the benefactress good morning. POTÁPYCH. You'd better not come.
15: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. What do you say, Potápych? God preserve me! POTÁPYCH. What's that! No matter how much you swear, I know you! For instance, why are you coming to the mistress now?
14: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. I wish you well, Potápych. POTÁPYCH. No need for it! [ Silence ] But you keep upsetting the mistress so! If you'd only put in a word for us when she's in a good humor; but you just look for the wrong time, in order to complain of us.
13: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. Of course, Potápych, you're an old man, why shouldn't you take a drink once in a while? POTÁPYCH. Sure, I guess I work for it.
12: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. You haven't any money for anything else; but you have for such things. POTÁPYCH. Well, anyhow, it ain't your business.
11: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. Your head aches. POTÁPYCH. Did you put up the money?
10: VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA. Result of yesterday evening, I suppose, my friend? POTÁPYCH. Wha-a-t?
9: [Footnote 1: The whole scene in a whisper.] POTÁPYCH is leaning against the door-jamb, his hand to his head. VASILÍSA PEREGRÍNOVNA enters quietly.
8: [ They kiss and go out in different directions. Same room as in second picture
7: NÁDYA. Do you love me? LEONÍD. I do love you, indeed I do!
6: LEONÍD. Good-by, then! Slowly, as if unwillingly, they separate. NÁDYA returns, overtakes LEONÍD and gazes into his eyes.
5: NÁDYA. What do you mean? LEONÍD. Little Nádya! [ He whispers in her ear.
4: LÍZA. My dear girl, don't carry your head too high! LEONÍD. Nádya! [NÁDYA goes to him ] Oh, Nádya, what a vile, good-for-nothing fellow I am!
3: LÍZA. [ Loudly ] Nádya! NÁDYA. [ Goes up to LÍZA. LEONÍD sits down upon the bench ] What's the matter?
2: LÍZA. What's the matter, don't you hear? NÁDYA. If I can't come, I'll send a note somehow or other.
1: LÍZA. What have you done, what have you done!… NÁDYA. [ Not listening to her, softly to LEONÍD] You will come to-morrow?
0: LEONÍD and NÁDYA reach the shore and disembark from the boat. LÍZA, NÁDYA, and LEONÍD
